assign.outcome:
**A layout system that doesn't fail, and why the current feedback never got there.** Landed: **[/imagine/design/system/](/imagine/design/system/)** — a proposal, not a change; nothing in `framework/core/` or `ext/DesignTool/` was touched.

![the page at 3440](/framework/ai/2026-09-01/system-proposal/system-3440.jpg)

**The system, in one sentence.** A page declares what it **holds** — `one` (a single read) · `many` (a repeating set) · `parts` (unlike regions used together), usually *inferred* from `children`, written only to override — and the room goes to **tracks, then regions, then scale**, with scale never optional, so there is no leftover. Four floors make the cramped side impossible: padding `clamp(0.5em, 6%, 3em)`, measure declared in *characters* (52–68) rather than ems, four gap rungs and only four, tracks floored at `min(14rem, 100%)`. The load-bearing idea: `--measure` is an `em`, so **scaling type is how a `one` page spends a widescreen** — a 3440 screen gets a 1024px column of large type at the same character count, and widening (which `widescreen.md` rightly forbids) never happens.

**The critique — top three of six on the page.** (1) No page ever says what it MEANT, so the tool grades outcome against a site average; `widescreen.md` itself says a dead-space finding asks *"is there a second thing the reader wants beside it?"* — a question only the page can answer and no page has a word for. (2) **The 'proper design' already exists and only the generator can read it**: `taste/ranges.js` exports `AUTHOR` — *"what to WRITE so the measurement lands in the band"* (pad 0.8–1.4em, gap 0.6–1.6em, measure 27–34em, rail 12–17em, tracks 1–3) — consumed solely by `styles/layouts/space/gen.js`. (3) A weighted mean of eleven bands averages away the one band that failed: `/imagine/gallery/` scores zero on `width-used` (0.132 vs an `ok` floor of 0.28, weight 8 of 62) and passes the rest — 87% "good", 13% of a 3440 screen.

**The pilot (~6h total, on the page).** 1 · `holds: "one"` on `/notes/git-branch-names/` (~1h) — scale spends the leftover with zero layout change. 2 · one new column width word, `grow`, plus `holds: "many"` on `/imagine/gallery/` (~2h) — closes the layout study's handoff gap #1. 3 · `check(page)` beside `analyze()`/`rate()` (~3h) — reads `page.holds`, asserts declaration == outcome, pass/fail, no score.

**Verified on itself.** 87/B at 1280, 94/A at 3440, no `high` findings, no horizontal scroll at either width — after two real self-inflicted bugs the tool caught: the house `auto-fill` gave two code sketches 480px tracks with five empty ones beside them at 3440 (fixed with `auto-fit` + an em ceiling — the exemption `layout-system.md` names but does not spell out; logged to the `layout` skill), and six callout boxes with a `border-inline-start` and one-sided padding read as `cramped · high`, the exact false positive tonight's [padding study](/imagine/design/padding/) named.

**Deliberately left:** no code written — `holds`, the `grow` width word and `check()` are all proposals (the brief forbade surgery, and each is a `Page`/`Page.css`/DesignTool API change the owner should approve); the audit was not re-run (its baseline is still `2026-08-17`, 338 rows, which is itself finding 6); no number was invented for `--measure` — the proposal moves the source of truth to the character count and lets the em be tuned until it measures.
